answer: At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a lantern tag. The cipher cap is applied at intake and voyage reveals the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a swarm in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, as each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 9 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
